name: Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Library for Recommendation
description: Recently, recommender system has achieved significant success. However, due to the openness of recommender systems, they remain vulnerable to malicious attacks. Additionally, natural noise in training data and issues such as data sparsity can also degrade the performance of recommender systems. Therefore, enhancing the robustness of recommender systems has become an increasingly important research topic. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive overview of the robustness of recommender systems. Based on our investigation, we categorize the robustness of recommender systems into adversarial robustness and non-adversarial robustness. In the adversarial robustness, we introduce the fundamental principles and classical methods of recommender system adversarial attacks and defenses. In the non-adversarial robustness, we analyze non-adversarial robustness from the perspectives of data sparsity, natural noise, and data imbalance. reputation: A survey-style library/benchmarking resource for robustness in recommender systems rather than a single standardized leaderboard benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark/resource; covers adversarial and non-adversarial robustness, but does not appear to define one canonical metric or fixed public score range.
